label: Wedding fertility relation (bad)
summary: Removes the scripted relationship named wedding_bad_fertility between the character and the target character.
details: The game's documentation only says it removes a scripted relationship. What the relationship means is not documented here beyond its name.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The other character in the relationship.

label: Wedding fertility relation (good)
summary: Removes the scripted relationship named wedding_good_fertility between the character and the target character.
details: The game's documentation only says it removes a scripted relationship. What the relationship means is not documented here beyond its name.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The other character in the relationship.

label: Wedding fertility relation (very bad)
summary: Removes the scripted relationship named wedding_very_bad_fertility between the character and the target character.
details: Vanilla uses it once, with the target given as a scope reference (`prev`). The game's documentation does not explain what the relationship means beyond its name.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The other character in the relationship.
fields.values: a character, or a reference such as `prev`

label: Wedding fertility relation (very good)
summary: Removes the scripted relationship named wedding_very_good_fertility between the character and the target character.
details: The game's documentation only says it removes a scripted relationship. What the relationship means is not documented here beyond its name.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The other character in the relationship.

label: Wet nurse relation
summary: Ends the relation in which the given character is the character's wet nurse.
details: The corresponding nursed child relation on the other side is removed with it (the game's relation definitions pair the two).

fields.name: target
fields.text: The other character in the relationship.

label: Religious head challenger
summary: Removes a title from the faith's list of challengers to its religious head.
details: Runs on a faith. The value is the title to remove. Vanilla uses it once, with a saved scope (`scope:pam_title_to_destroy`).

label: Religious head title
summary: Removes the faith's religious head title, so the faith no longer has one.
details: Runs on a faith. Written as `yes`. Vanilla uses it ten times.

label: Reserved gold
summary: Takes gold from the character, drawing first on the part the AI has set aside as its reserved budget.
details: Whatever the reserved budget cannot cover is taken from the rest of the character's gold. The game's documentation does not show how the amount is written.

label: Reserved treasury
summary: Takes treasury from the character, drawing first on the part the AI has set aside as its reserved budget.
details: Whatever the reserved budget cannot cover is taken from the rest of the treasury. The game's documentation does not show how the amount is written.

label: Rite culture
summary: Takes a culture off the list of cultures tied to the rite.
details: Runs on a rite. The target is the culture to remove.

label: Rite doctrine
summary: Takes a doctrine away from the rite.
details: Runs on a rite. Vanilla uses it with anointment doctrines, for example `doctrine_no_anointment`.

label: Rite tenet
summary: Takes a tenet away from the rite.
details: Runs on a rite. Vanilla gives the tenet by key (`tenet:tenet_pacifism`) or as a saved scope.

label: Saint
summary: Takes a character off the faith's list of saints.
details: Runs on a faith. The target is the character to remove.

label: Sanctified for faith
summary: Removes an artifact's sanctification for the given faith.
details: Runs on an artifact. The target is the faith, for example `faith:catholic`.

label: Scheme cooldown
summary: Lets the character start a scheme against the target character again by removing the cooldown that blocks it.
details: The cooldown only applies to that one scheme type against that one target.

fields.name: scheme
fields.text: Which scheme type the cooldown is for.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The character the scheme would be aimed at.

label: Scheme modifier
summary: Removes a named modifier from a scheme.
details: Vanilla uses it 21 times, for example to take away the tiered `scheme_end_buff` modifiers.

label: Secret
summary: Removes the secret so it no longer exists.
details: Runs on a secret. Written as `yes`.

label: Gold (short-term budget)
summary: Takes gold from the character, drawing first on the part the AI has set aside as its short-term budget.
details: Whatever that budget cannot cover is taken from the rest of the gold. Vanilla gives a number, a gold value such as `minor_gold_value`, or a block with `value` plus `multiply`, `add`, `divide`, `min` or `max`. Vanilla also uses a range such as `{ 10 20 }`.

fields.name: value
fields.values: a number, a script value, or a block

label: Treasury (short-term budget)
summary: Takes treasury from the character, drawing first on the part the AI has set aside as its short-term budget.
details: Whatever that budget cannot cover is taken from the rest of the treasury. Vanilla gives treasury values such as `minor_treasury_value`.

label: Faction special character
summary: Removes the faction's special character.
details: Runs on a faction.

label: Faction special title
summary: Removes the faction's special title, going by its name.
details: The game's documentation repeats the text of remove_special_character and says it removes the special character, which does not match the key's name. Which one it removes is not certain.

label: Tenet
summary: Takes a tenet away from the faith.
details: Runs on a faith. Vanilla uses it with keys such as `tenet_astrology` or `tenet_christian_syncretism`.

label: Important location title
summary: Makes the county no longer count as an important location for the target title.
details: Runs on a county title. The target is the title it stops being important for.

label: Title law
summary: Removes a law from the title without paying any removal costs or applying any removal effects.
details: This leaves the law's group empty, so use it only when you are getting rid of a whole law group. Vanilla uses it with laws such as `male_only_law`. It works on a title; the law is written by its key.

label: Title law (with effects)
summary: Removes a law from the title and applies the law's removal costs and effects.
details: This leaves the law's group empty, so use it only when you are getting rid of a whole law group. The documented usage line names remove_title_law, which looks like a copy mistake.

label: Trait
summary: Takes a trait away from the character.
details: If the character does not have the trait, no tooltip is shown. Vanilla uses it about 900 times, usually with a trait key such as `callous`.

label: Trait (always show tooltip)
summary: Takes a trait away from the character.
details: The difference from remove_trait: the tooltip is shown even if the character does not have the trait. Vanilla uses it for illnesses such as `cancer` and `typhus`.

label: Travel option
summary: Removes the named travel option from the travel plan.
details: Runs on a travel plan.

label: Travel plan modifier
summary: Removes a named modifier from the travel plan.
details: Vanilla uses it once, for `preserved_wilderness_travel_modifier`.

label: Travel point of interest
summary: Removes a type of travel point of interest from the province.
details: Runs on a province. Written with the point of interest type.

label: Treasury
summary: Takes treasury from the character.
details: Vanilla gives a script value, a saved scope, or a block with `value`, which can itself be a block with `add`. It uses values such as `minor_treasury_value`.

fields.name: value
fields.values: a script value, or a block

label: Treasury or gold
summary: Takes the amount from the character's treasury if they have one, and from their gold if not.
details: Vanilla uses it about 190 times, mostly with values such as `medium_treasury_or_gold_value`. A block form with `value` plus `multiply`, `add`, `min` or `max` is also used.

fields.name: value
fields.values: a number, a script value, or a block

label: Variable
summary: Removes a variable.
details: The variable is given by its name. The input does not say which scopes it runs on. Vanilla uses it about 1700 times, for example with `contest_aptitude`.

label: Gold (war chest budget)
summary: Takes gold from the character, drawing first on the part the AI has set aside as its war chest budget.
details: Whatever that budget cannot cover is taken from the rest of the gold.

label: Treasury (war chest budget)
summary: Takes treasury from the character, drawing first on the part the AI has set aside as its war chest budget.
details: Whatever that budget cannot cover is taken from the rest of the treasury.

label: Worst personal tenet
summary: Removes the character's personal tenet that gives the least spiritual fulfillment.
details: Works on a playable character. If the character has no personal tenets, it does nothing and gives no error. Written as `yes`.

label: Replace building
summary: Replaces a building in the province's holding with a new one.
details: For special buildings (duchy capital, special building, great building) it creates the slot and the building even if no building of that type exists. For regular buildings, a building of the same type must already be there, or it fails with an error. Duchy capital buildings are not created if the province does not support them. Vanilla uses it once, with `celestial_great_barracks_01`.

label: Replace court position
summary: Takes a court position from its current holder and gives it to another character, in the scoped character's court.
details: The old holder loses the position and the recipient receives it.

fields.name: recipient
fields.text: The character who gets the position.

fields.name: holder
fields.text: The character who loses the position.

label: Reset beneficiary
summary: Makes the character stop having a beneficiary.
details: Written as `yes`.

label: Reset coat of arms
summary: Puts the coat of arms back to its template.
details: Works on a title, a dynasty, a house, an organization or a confederation. Written as `yes`.
